# DistilBERT sweep — WELFake (generated by `python -m src.models.distilbert --render`)

`distilbert-base-uncased`, input = title [SEP] text (head truncation), AdamW + linear schedule, warmup ratio 0.1, weight decay 0.01, fp16, 3 epochs with the best epoch (val macro-F1) kept, seed 42. Sweep = 20,000-row stratified subset of WELFake train, evaluated on the full WELFake val split (6,080). Selection metric: val macro-F1. Per-run logs: `docs/results/train_logs/distilbert_sweep_*.json`.

| run | lr | max_len | batch × accum | best epoch / 3 | warmup | seed | val macro-F1 (best ep.) | val acc | per-epoch val macro-F1 | minutes | peak GPU GiB | hardware |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sweep 20k (20000) | 2e-05 | 256 | 16 × 1 | 3 | 0.1 | 42 | **0.9869** | 0.9872 | 0.9792 → 0.9807 → 0.9869 | 14.8 | 1.68 | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2050 |
| sweep 20k (20000) | 3e-05 | 256 | 16 × 1 | 3 | 0.1 | 42 | **0.9863** | 0.9865 | 0.9826 → 0.9854 → 0.9863 | 14.3 | 1.68 | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2050 |
| **best completed** sweep 20k (20000) | 5e-05 | 256 | 16 × 1 | 3 | 0.1 | 42 | **0.9871** | 0.9873 | 0.9792 → 0.9870 → 0.9871 | 15.2 | 1.69 | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2050 |
| sweep 20k | 2e-05 | 512 | 8 × 2 | not run (stopped on user decision, 2026-10-26; the max_len 512 arm stays deferred at ESE) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| sweep 20k | 3e-05 | 512 | 8 × 2 | not run (stopped on user decision, 2026-10-26; the max_len 512 arm stays deferred at ESE) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| sweep 20k | 5e-05 | 512 | 8 × 2 | not run (stopped on user decision, 2026-10-26; the max_len 512 arm stays deferred at ESE) |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| **full train** (48639) | 5e-05 | 256 | 16 × 1 | 3 | 0.1 | 42 | **0.9930** | 0.9931 | 0.9870 → 0.9906 → 0.9930 | 31.6 | 1.68 | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2050 |

**Best completed run:** lr = 5e-05, max_len = 256 (val macro-F1 0.9871 at epoch 3). Only 3 of 6 configs ran (max_len 256 only), so this is the best of the completed runs, not a full-sweep winner.
The final model `data/models/distilbert-welfake-v1/` was retrained on the full train split with this config (sweep winner `distilbert_sweep_lr5e-05_len256`; the full-train config equals the winner): best epoch 3, val macro-F1 0.9930, 31.6 min.

**lr = 5e-5:** at max_len 256 it fits the 20k subset fastest (train loss 0.0077 at epoch 3 vs 0.0153 / 0.0105 for 2e-5 / 3e-5) and its val loss rises from epoch 2 (0.0572) to epoch 3 (0.0671), i.e. it starts to overfit, while val macro-F1 stays flat (0.9870 -> 0.9871); it ties lr 2e-5 (0.9869) within 0.0002 — no lr is clearly better at 256.

## Held-out test (final model, threshold 0.5) — `train_logs/distilbert_welfake_v1_test.json`

| test split | n | accuracy | macro-F1 | P_fake | R_fake | ROC-AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| welfake | 6080 | 0.9900 | 0.9898 | 0.9947 | 0.9823 | 0.9995 |
| isot | 3757 | 0.9992 | 0.9992 | 0.9994 | 0.9988 | 1.0000 |

ISOT test is in-domain, not cross-dataset (ISOT ⊂ WELFake; ~80 % of ISOT test rows are in WELFake train).

## Published reference points (other work) — not our measurement

Numbers copied from the cited sources; we did not reproduce any of them. They are **not directly comparable** to ours: those works use raw WELFake / ISOT with their own random splits, no Reuters-dateline / credit / caption artefact stripping and no cross-corpus de-duplication (ISOT ⊂ WELFake), so their scores may include the boiler-plate leakage our preprocessing removes.

| source | model | dataset / split | metric | published value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Verma et al. 2021, IEEE TCSS 8(4) (WELFake paper; abstract) | WELFake (word embedding over linguistic features) | WELFake | accuracy | 96.73 % (reported as +1.31 % over BERT, +4.25 % over CNN) |
| Abdo & Roki 2026, IJCA 187(119), Table 4 | DistilBERT-base (lr 3e-5, 5 ep., batch 32, max_len 512) | WELFake, stratified 80/10/10, test n = 7,214 | accuracy / macro-F1 | 95.38 % / 0.9538 |
| Abdo & Roki 2026, IJCA 187(119), Table 4 | BERT-base (lr 2e-5, 4 ep.) | same | accuracy / macro-F1 | 95.92 % / 0.9592 |
| Abdo & Roki 2026, IJCA 187(119), Table 4 | RoBERTa-base (lr 2e-5, 4 ep.) | same | accuracy / macro-F1 | 96.84 % / 0.9684 |
| Blackledge & Atapour-Abarghouei 2021, arXiv:2109.09796, Table II | DistilBERT / BERT / DeBERTa | ISOT, 80 % train / 10 % test | accuracy (F1) | 0.989 (0.989) / 0.990 (0.989) / 0.997 (0.989) |
| same, Table IV | DistilBERT / BERT / DeBERTa | train ISOT → test Combined Corpus (Khan et al.) | accuracy (F1) | 0.670 (0.655) / 0.670 (0.702) / 0.697 (0.695) |
| same, Table V | DistilBERT / BERT / DeBERTa | train Combined Corpus → test ISOT | accuracy (F1) | 0.775 (0.750) / 0.670 (0.610) / 0.730 (0.695) |

Sources: <https://c3.itec.aau.at/?p=138> (WELFake abstract; DOI 10.1109/TCSS.2021.3068519), <https://ijcaonline.org/archives/volume187/number119/abdo-ijca-2026-464629276ffa.pdf>, <https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.09796>. Our deferred DistilBERT test cells above stay "deferred to ESE"; these rows do not fill them. The published in-domain → cross-corpus drop (≈ 0.99 → 0.66–0.78 accuracy) matches the direction of our expected† cross-dataset result, but the Combined Corpus is not our WELFake∖ISOT split.
